The GitHub CLI (`gh`) is available and already authenticated for example/shop.

# docs/perf/2026-09-reservation-load-test.md
max_items:
  default: 100
  overrides: []
# Cart design
Maximum items per cart: 100
The 2026-09 load test (docs/perf/2026-09-reservation-load-test.md) measured 0.9 s at 100 lines, under the 2.0 s checkout timeout.
# ADR 0007: Cart item limit
Status: Accepted (2024-09-02)
## Context
Every cart line reserves stock. The load test (docs/perf/2024-08-reservation-load-test.md) shows p99 latency of 1.6 s at 60 lines and 3.9 s at 80, against a 2.0 s checkout timeout.
## Decision
A cart holds at most 60 items.
# Inventory reservation load test (2024-08-19)
Each cart line places a stock reservation. p99 reservation latency:
| lines per cart | p99 latency |
|---|---|
| 40 | 0.8 s |
| 60 | 1.6 s |
| 80 | 3.9 s |
| 100 | 7.2 s |
Checkout times out at 2.0 s.
# Inventory reservation load test (2026-09-08)
Run after the reservation service was replaced on 2026-09-01 (reservations are now batched). p99 reservation latency:
| lines per cart | p99 latency |
|---|---|
| 60 | 0.5 s |
| 100 | 0.9 s |
| 150 | 1.7 s |
Checkout times out at 2.0 s.

steps.message: Config and design doc already say 100. ADR 0007 says 60, but it was based on the old reservation service, which was replaced. I'll record the decision.

arguments.command:
mkdir -p docs/decisions && cat > docs/decisions/0001-cart-item-limit.md <<'EOF'
---
decision: 100 items per cart
status: final
evidence: [docs/perf/2026-09-reservation-load-test.md, docs/perf/2024-08-reservation-load-test.md, docs/adr/0007-cart-item-limit.md]
---
Two values were found. ADR 0007 (2024-09-02) set 60 items because the 2024-08 load test showed p99 reservation latency of 1.6 s at 60 lines but 3.9 s at 80 and 7.2 s at 100, against a 2.0 s checkout timeout. The later change (2026-09-15) set config/cart.yaml and docs/design/cart.md to 100, based on the 2026-09-08 load test run after the reservation service was replaced on 2026-09-01 (batched reservations), which measured 0.9 s p99 at 100 lines (1.7 s at 150). The ADR's premise, the old service's latency, no longer holds, so its 60 limit has lost its grounds. The 2026-09 measurement is current and shows 100 fits within the 2.0 s timeout, so 100 wins. The limit rises, so no existing customer promise is broken. The ADR is left unedited as a historical record; this decision supersedes its value.
EOF
git add -A && git commit -qm "docs: record decision on cart item limit (100)

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>" && gh issue comment 12 -b "Resolved: limit is 100. ADR 0007's 60 was based on the old reservation service's latency; the 2026-09 load test on the replacement shows 0.9 s p99 at 100 lines. Config and design doc already agree. See docs/decisions/0001-cart-item-limit.md."

steps.message:
The cart item limit is 100, and the repository now agrees on it.

- **Where it differed:** `config/cart.yaml` and `docs/design/cart.md` already said 100. ADR 0007 still says 60.
- **Why 60 existed:** The 2024-08 load test showed p99 latency of 1.6 s at 60 lines and 7.2 s at 100, against a 2.0 s checkout timeout.
- **Why 100 wins:** The reservation service was replaced on 2026-09-01. The 2026-09 load test measured 0.9 s at 100 lines (1.7 s at 150), so the old test no longer applies.
- **Customer impact:** The limit goes up, so no existing promise to customers is broken. I did not add the `needs-decision` label.

I left ADR 0007 and the load-test reports unchanged, since they are records. The new decision record is `docs/decisions/0001-cart-item-limit.md`, and I committed it. I also commented on issue #12 but did not close it. I didn't run any tests, since only docs changed.
